claim: McKinsey (5,554) and BCG (4,873) file H-1B labor condition applications at similar volumes; Bain (1,108) files about a fifth as many as McKinsey (FY2015-2025, certified).
method: Count of certified LCA filings by firm, FY2015-2025 (src/metrics.py: hiring)
limitation: H-1B filings are a proxy for US hiring of foreign nationals, not headcount or revenue; differences also reflect each firm's immigration practice

claim: Between FY2016 and FY2024 McKinsey's certified filings grew 12.5% a year, BCG's 10.4% and Bain's 2.2%.
method: Endpoint CAGR of certified LCA filings, FY2016 to FY2024
limitation: Two-endpoint growth rate; FY2026 partial and excluded; filing practice differs by firm

claim: McKinsey's filings span 45 worksite states and 155 cities, BCG's 35 and 57, Bain's 19 and 32.
method: Distinct worksite states and cities in certified filings, FY2015-2025
limitation: Worksites of sponsored workers only, not every office

claim: Bain's positions are the most concentrated by state (HHI 0.138) versus BCG (0.091) and McKinsey (0.075).
method: Herfindahl-Hirschman index of state shares of certified positions
limitation: Positions are batched in filings (McKinsey files up to 100 at once), which affects weights

claim: McKinsey requests 7.9 worker positions per filing on average versus 1.8 for BCG and 2.5 for Bain, so position totals are not comparable across firms.
method: Mean positions per filing, all statuses, FY2015-2025
limitation: A filing-practice difference as much as a hiring difference

claim: Median offered base wage in certified filings: BCG $165,000, Bain $152,000, McKinsey $150,000.
method: Median of annualized offered wage, FY2015-2025
limitation: Offered base wage excludes bonuses; wages outside $30K-$1M dropped

claim: Technical occupations (SOC 15) account for 35.9% of McKinsey's certified filings, 20.3% of BCG's and 5.2% of Bain's.
method: Share of certified filings in SOC major group 15, FY2015-2025
limitation: Share of sponsored filings, not of the firm's total workforce

claim: The technical share of filings rose at all three firms between FY2015-19 and FY2021-25 (McKinsey 31.8% to 38.0%, BCG 14.5% to 24.0%, Bain 1.6% to 8.8%).
method: Technical share by period
limitation: Bain's counts are small (12 technical filings in FY2025) so its share is volatile

claim: Direct US federal prime contract awards FY2015-2024: McKinsey 188 awards worth $762M, BCG 127 worth $826M; none found for Bain.
method: Count and sum of prime awards with start year FY2015-2024 and value > 0
limitation: Prime federal contracts only; 'none found' is not proof Bain has no public-sector work; awards dated by start year

claim: The Department of Defense accounts for 68.3% of BCG's federal contract value and 53.1% of McKinsey's; McKinsey sells to 19 agencies versus 10 for BCG.
method: Share of award value by awarding agency; distinct agencies
limitation: Reflects where contract-based consulting is procured as well as firm focus

claim: As subcontractors, McKinsey holds 128 federal subawards ($1,056M, dominated by one large award), BCG 55 ($107M) and Bain 3 ($8.4M).
method: Count and sum of subawards, FY2015-2024
limitation: A single large McKinsey subaward dominates the total; subaward reporting is incomplete

claim: BCG's reported revenue grew 9.8% a year from 2018 to 2025 and its reported headcount 8.9% a year.
method: CAGR between reported endpoint values (2018, 2025)
limitation: Two endpoints only; 2021 and 2022 revenue not located

claim: In 2023 McKinsey's estimated revenue (about $16B) and headcount (about 45,000) exceeded BCG's reported $12.3B and 32,000; Bain's estimates are about $6B and 19,000.
method: 2023 points from data/manual/firm_scale_points.csv
limitation: McKinsey and Bain are third-party estimates; Bain rated low confidence

claim: Estimated 2023 revenue per employee: BCG $384K, McKinsey $356K, Bain $316K.
method: 2023 revenue divided by 2023 headcount
limitation: Inherits estimate error for McKinsey and Bain

claim: Only BCG has a reported, source-verified scale series (18 reported points); McKinsey has 0 reported points and Bain 5, so a decade-long revenue comparison across the three firms is not possible from public data.
method: Count of reported and verified rows in firm_scale_points.csv
limitation: Coverage gap in this study as well as in public disclosure

claim: BCG's sitemap lists 110 core city office pages and Bain's 69, consistent with the firms' own '100+ cities' and '67 cities' statements.
method: Count of core city office pages in the public sitemap
limitation: Page counts are not an audited office list; McKinsey not covered

claim: The largest US employee count the firms reported on PERM filings in FY2024 was McKinsey 9,000, BCG 7,780 and Bain 3,900; since FY2016 BCG grew 9.4% a year, Bain 8.0% and McKinsey 3.2%.
method: Yearly maximum of employer_num_employees on PERM filings, FY2016 to FY2024
limitation: Filer-defined, unaudited and rounded (McKinsey); FY2025+ not used (form change)

claim: PERM cases are certified 98.1% of the time for McKinsey, 88.5% for Bain and 85.3% for BCG, which has 14.1% withdrawn.
method: Share of cases by outcome, FY2015-2026
limitation: Why BCG withdraws more cases is not in the data

claim: India is the largest citizenship among sponsored workers at all three firms (36.5% McKinsey, 30.0% BCG, 21.5% Bain).
method: Share of filings with a citizenship value
limitation: Sponsored foreign nationals only

claim: SEC filings name McKinsey far more often (21,583 filings, 2015-2025) than BCG (10,065) or Bain (9,506); the industry mix of operating-company filers naming each firm is nearly identical (HHI 0.177, 0.176, 0.173).
method: Distinct filings from EDGAR full-text search; HHI of industry shares among operating-company filings
limitation: A mention is not an engagement; names also appear in cited studies and director biographies; mix mostly reflects the SEC filer universe

claim: BCG's industry section lists 170 pages and Bain's 121; BCG's capability section lists 292 pages versus Bain's 163.
method: Page counts under industry and capability URL sections, mapped to a common taxonomy
limitation: Published-content emphasis, not revenue share; McKinsey not covered

claim: UK public-sector contract awards 2015-2025 (excluding framework ceilings): McKinsey 135 awards worth GBP 308M, BCG 108 worth GBP 270M; none found for Bain.
method: Contracts Finder awarded notices, supplier matched by name, award year 2015-2025, value under GBP 50M
limitation: Notices above the publication threshold only; 'none found' is not proof of no UK work

claim: BCG's dated publication pages rose from 202 in 2013 to 650 in 2025, and pages whose URL names AI or GenAI went from 3.4% of the year's pages in 2019 to 18.5% in 2025.
method: Count of /publications/YYYY/ URLs; share with an AI term in the slug
limitation: Page count is not research quality or revenue; slug keywords undercount AI content; McKinsey and Bain not covered

claim: OpenAlex records 799 scholarly works for McKinsey affiliations and 876 for BCG (2010-2025); it has no record for Bain.
method: Works with a firm institution affiliation
limitation: Reflects affiliation recording, not total research output

claim: Canadian federal contracts over CAD 10K, 2015-2025: McKinsey 34 contracts worth CAD 121M, BCG 15 worth CAD 45M; none found for Bain.
method: Proactive-disclosure contracts CSV filtered by vendor name with the shared strict matcher; contract year 2015-2025
limitation: Contracts over CAD 10,000 only; values include amendments as reported; 'none found' is not proof of no Canadian work

claim: Australian federal contract notices 2015-2025: BCG 195 notices worth AUD 284M, McKinsey 15 worth AUD 21M; none found for Bain.
method: Every AusTender OCDS contract notice published 2015-2025 paged by week and filtered by supplier name with the shared strict matcher
limitation: Notified values above reporting thresholds; one very large BCG notice in 2024 dominates that year; 'none found' is not proof of no Australian work
